evidence.summary: Changes route only the exact Z690-I profile into existing internal headless build/install. GPU algorithms unchanged. GPT identity checked before effects. Source inventories and child hashes retained; normalize ordering only and reject duplicate/missing input. Existing registration saves BCD and verifies unrelated entries; recovery restores Windows first without package. Storage prep verifies exact disk/GUID/geometry, backs up BCD/loader, shrinks NTFS via native API and formats only a newly created partition. Apply refuses repeat geometry. Failed storage operations stop with phase receipt, no blind deletion. Windows EFI/recovery, original menu prefix, USB files and GPU runtime guards are preservation boundaries. EFI boot can still fail; physical acceptance is explicitly pending. Input inventory enumerates every runtime .c/.h/.ps1 outside build directories, all EDK2 include headers, local-config, assets.json, PowerShell headless builder, optional Python builder, plus generated child contract. Exact path/hash sets and count are compared; duplicates cannot replace a required path. Configure resolves enum to exact board/BIOS, and validates native partition/volume identity; installer rechecks those live values and encryption/SecureBoot plus package hashes. Runtime uses GPT device path GUID and existing hardware/graph guards, not display output. Host tests exercise production sources but mock real firmware operations; deployment runs actual native queries. No-change retains proven USB route but fails the owner request to remove USB dependence.

evidence.summary: Read-only live inspection: old Windows ESP100MiB has ~63MiB free, assets ~81MiB; existing installer requires >=1GiB. C on Samsung990PRO4TB has ~2TiB free, native shrink supported, BitLocker off. Dedicated1GiB partition4 created by shrinking C 1GiB+859136 bytes for alignment. Receipt verifies Windows ESP/recovery geometry and bootmgfw SHA unchanged, firmware enum unchanged. No-change retains USB dependence; using old ESP cannot fit assets; dedicated system-SSD ESP satisfies installer. This adds partitioning/UEFI risk; current claim is preparation/installation, not cold-boot success.
